title: R-CAL judge calibration: viability-necessity clause + systematic-bias diagnostic
data_grounding: R142 one-shot diagnostic (auditor recompute): every healthy judge misses ONLY on baseline-prefer pairs (over_novel(a1|baseline)=3, over_cons(baseline|a1)=0) — a SYSTEMATIC novelty-over-weighting bias; inter-judge Cohen kappa=0.628 (>=0.6), proportion agreement 0.867 (judges are internally consistent). kappa-vs-labels=0.5. The defect is the judge prompt under-weighting feasibility/testability, NOT random noise.
amendment: (1) The R-CAL judge prompt MUST enforce VIABILITY-NECESSITY: a mechanism that is infeasible or untestable AS WRITTEN is NOT preferred, regardless of novelty (an invention must be viable AND non-obvious; novelty alone never wins). (2) Qualification adds a systematic-bias check: |over_novel - over_cons| <= 1 (no systematic novelty-over-weighting). (3) The acc>=0.8 AND answered>=0.9 bar is UNCHANGED; inter-judge alpha>=0.6 required. (4) Forward-only: applies to a FRESH one-shot corpus (r143); the burned r142 outcome stands (Art.7).
not_gaming: This is a calibration fix grounded in a measured systematic bias, not a bar-lowering: the acc>=0.8 bar stays; the prompt encodes a GENERAL principle (viability necessary) tested on NEW pairs. Art.3/8 respected.
